criteria.evidence: Direct Windows GPU-process counters summed across all VM processes and instances show a peak of 13,485,330,432 dedicated bytes during the case. The broader all-stage summed GPU-related committed peak, including shared system memory, is 13,616,123,904 bytes. Both are below the decimal-byte limit. There were 435 valid case samples, no recorded sampling errors, and a maximum gap of about 2.599 seconds. The stopped VM dedicated counter was 24,059,904 bytes both before and after; the measured model-load increase was 13,461,270,528 bytes. The model and MTP allocations are contained in the measured VM, so this conservative containing-VM total is a defensible upper bound for those allocations under the observed workload. It is not an exact isolated-model value or a continuous-time peak.

The inspected analyzer requires vmwp identities, counters whose PIDs match those identities, unique instance names, valid nonnegative byte fields, stopped baselines, a minimum load increase, and a maximum sampling gap. It sums all instances without alias deduplication or desktop-baseline subtraction. The raw replay checked all 520 rows and matched the persisted analysis. Summing aliases/shared resources can overcount, which is conservative for the stated upper-bound inference. Windows counter overreporting remains a documented caveat.

The captured profile uses Qwen3.8-27B IQ3_XXS with embedded shared MTP, GPU layers 99, no CPU offload, context 69,888, a 65,536 Sift target, and 2 draft tokens. Exact 65,536 input plus 4,096 output passed without truncation. The 256k and 1M context examples passed with different adaptive targets (32,193 and 65,536) and forwarded counts (32,053 and 33,300). Three native Claude tasks reconstructed to the archived artifacts and passed their validators; one used a bounded feedback repair, with the failed revision preserved. These results support the measured workload, not arbitrary future workloads or universal semantic retention.
